summary: The SYMLINK path-boundary class (decision 0028) is closed: a destination or ancestor symlink, a .. traversal, a .. that normalizes onto an in-target symlink, a symlink loop, and a crafted directory copy2 would treat as a container are all refused, in a preflight before the first mutation. copytree dereferences trusted source content into validated destinations rather than recreating outward source links. The anti-reopen scan resolves keyword args and module aliases, forbids bare imports of the primitives, guards both sides of rename/replace, and requires guarded_copytree — so a future raw write fails the suite.
residual_risks: HARD-LINK inode-aliasing (a regular file hard-linked to an outside inode; copy2 truncates the shared inode) is a distinct, deeper class beyond 0028's symlink scope, deliberately deferred to a follow-up (documented inline). Requires unlink-before-write / descriptor-relative I/O.

TOCTOU races (a concurrent writer swapping a validated path for an outward symlink between check and write) are inherent to all path-based validation and pre-existing; deferred to the same follow-up. Requires descriptor-relative (openat/O_NOFOLLOW) I/O.
recommendation: approve — the deferred classes are documented and out of the accepted scope
